headlines.title: Investigation underway outside Pittsburg Police Department
headlines.description: An investigation is underway Thursday outside the Pittsburg Police Department, where a large law enforcement presence can be seen with police tape sealing off the front entrance of the building. Contra Costa County Fire Protection District said crews were dispatched to a medical aid call at the police department at 65 Civic Avenue. No other information was immediately available.

headlines.title: Preliminary 3.3 magnitude earthquake strikes near Santa Rosa
headlines.description: A 3.3 magnitude earthquake struck near Santa Rosa, according to the United States Geological Survey. The quake hit at 10:33 a.m. Thursday and was centered four miles north of the Sonoma County city, the USGS said. The temblor was initially reported as a 3.5 magnitude. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates. headlines.title: New numbers show odds spike for major Bay Area earthquake in next 30 years
headlines.description: The risk of a large earthquake in the Bay Area has just been recalculated, and the odds have gone up, according to a recalibrated prediction from the U.S. Geological Survey. New federal numbers put the odds of a magnitude 6.7 quake or stronger in the Bay Area during the next 30 years at 74% — up from 72% in 2014 at the time of the previous prediction. These updated predictions were first reported by the San Francisco Chronicle, which requested updated data from the USGS. “It’s reinforcing what we already know,” United States Geological Survey geophysicist Kevin Milner said. “That we have to be prepared for a major earthquake. It is going to happen in most of our lifetimes.” Milner co-authored the first study and conducted the new one as well. He said the more time that passes without a major quake, the higher the probability of having one. Stanford University Aug 25 East Bay Aug 13 The Hayward-Rodgers Creek Fault System, which stretches from San Jose to the San Pablo Bay, still has the highest probability of the Bay Area faults of producing a magnitude 6.7 or stronger earthquake at 34%. But the biggest increase is on the San Andreas Fault, which the USGS placed at 25.5%, which is up 3.6% from 2014. The San Andreas Fault stretches from Southern California through the Bay Area and north toward Eureka. It also produced the devastating 1906 earthquake, as well as the Loma Prieta quake in 1989. As the earthquake risk rises, so does the potential for damage — especially to critical infrastructure. Victor Zayas, president of Earthquake Protection Systems, said while building standards have made major advances, more protections are needed. “If we build any buildings, especially any new hospitals, we should be building them to not be damaged by earthquakes, not just not collapse,” Zayas said. USGS is working on developing new models to better understand earthquakes and their risks.

headlines.title: Bicyclist dies after collision near Highway 101 in San Jose
headlines.description: A bicyclist was killed in a collision Thursday morning near Highway 101 in San Jose, according to police. The collision involving a vehicle and bicyclist happened around 7:45 a.m. in the area of Tully Road and the Highway 101 on-ramp. The bicyclist died from his injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene by medics, police said. The driver involved in the collision remained at the scene and is cooperating with the investigation. Westbound Tully Road from South King Road to the Highway 101 on-ramp is expected to remain closed for an extended period while police investigate. Drivers are being asked to avoid the area and use alternate routes. Additional information was not immediately available. This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

headlines.title: Women speak out after man posing as 49ers player tries to scam them
headlines.description: A pair of women who saw through the lies of a man pretending to be a 49ers player to scam other women came forward to speak out for the others who can’t or feel too ashamed to do it. The U.S. Attorney’s Office in Oregon says 35-year-old Daejon Love shared photos of him in 49ers uniforms or living lavishly online with women looking for love. This was part of what authorities said he used to scam dozens of women across Oregon, Washington, Idaho and California. One of those women was Dominque Dubose, who matched with Love on a dating app in 2025. “He had pictures on his profile, of him playing for the 49ers as an NFL receiver, I think wide receiver or something,” she said. But the receiver felt like a deceiver to Dubose. She immediately began investigating, eventually unearthing lie after lie. “I kind of called him out like I know you’re not who you say you are,” Dubose said. “And that’s when he stopped talking. I blocked him and because I didn’t want to contact him anymore.” The U.S. Attorney’s Office said Love would lure women in and later used 18-year-Old Taylor Chan, who posed as his financial advisor. Court documents say the scheme going from at least February 2022 until their arrests last month and went as far as creating fake bank accounts that appear to show their investments growing after they sent love money. Court documents say one woman lost more than $87,000. Collectively, the pair pocketed more than $1.3 million, authorities said. “Once they had no more money to invest, asked too many, or for related documentation, Love blocked communications with them, but kept their money.” Investigators say they’ve identified at least 26 women they believe were victims of Love and Chan’s elaborate scheme. Ayo Faye, who now lives in Southern California, says while living in San Jose in 2023, she matched with Love on a dating app and later met him at Westfield Valley Fair, where he showed up decked out in 49ers gear. “He quote on quote caught himself trying to prove that he was real or whatever and he has money by coming with all these bags,” she said. She said it ended abruptly when she wouldn’t send him any money. Both women say they’re now speaking out because they want Love and Chan to pay for their harm and manipulation and because other women can’t or feel too ashamed to. “It’s funny to some but for others it’s not for me I didn’t have to experience that so I can laugh here and there but at the end of the day I do know what the other women are going through and I couldn’t have imagined having to go through that,” Dubose said.

headlines.title: Man shot, killed in San Jose
headlines.description: A man was shot and killed in San Jose on Wednesday night and police are still trying to piece together what happened and why. Officers were sent to the 700 block of Stockton Avenue near Taylor Street at about 11 p.m. to investigate reports of a shooting, San Jose police said Thursday. When they got to the scene, officers found a man who had been shot at least once. He was taken to a hospital, where he later died, police said. The motive and circumstances surrounding the shooting are still under investigation. The victim’s name wasn’t released. It is the city’s 18th homicide of 2026. Anyone with information can contact Detective Sgt. Barragan at 4106@sanjoseca.gov or Detective Harrington at 4365@sanjoseca.gov or 408-277-5283. Bay City News contributed to this report
headlines.source: NBC Bay Area staff and Bay City News

headlines.title: Traveling for Labor Day? Expect to pay more this year
headlines.description: Millions of Americans are fitting in one last summer trip this Labor Day weekend, but travelers should expect to pay more whether they’re flying or hitting the road. Travel picked up Thursday, with the Federal Aviation Administration expecting it to be the busiest day for air travel over the holiday weekend with nearly 54,000 flights. The number of flights is expected to dip slightly Friday to fewer than 53,000. Saturday is expected to be a calmer travel day with fewer than 40,000 flights before air travel picks up again as people begin returning home. According to AAA, domestic flights are costing about 2% more this Labor Day weekend compared with last year, though fares to some popular destinations are up as much as 20%. As for hitting the road, more than 45 million people are expected to drive to their destinations for the three-day weekend. Most of those taking a road trip will be paying a premium to fill up gas tanks. AAA said as long as there is instability along the Strait of Hormuz, gas prices will remain high and unstable. The agency reports gas prices this weekend are $1.18 higher than the same time last year. headlines.title: San Jose's Regional Medical Center adds 20 ER beds amid growing demand
headlines.description: Regional Medical Center in San Jose is increasing its emergency room capacity by nearly 60% in an effort to reduce patient wait times. A new section of the emergency department opened Wednesday afternoon, adding 20 beds as part of a $17 million expansion project. Some of the new beds are in private rooms. The expansion brings the emergency department’s total capacity to 53 beds. The new beds are expected to fill up quickly. Regional Medical Center accounts for 30% of emergency room visits among hospitals operated by Santa Clara County. “These additional beds mean we can move patients in to get medications and treatments more quickly, decreasing their wait times and decreasing the wait for relief from their symptoms,” said Dr. Yvonne Karanas, physician executive at Regional Medical Center. County leaders said the additional capacity is needed as demand for emergency services at county hospitals continues to grow. Emergency department demand has increased 10% over the past two years and is expected to rise further. Santa Clara County Executive James Williams said cuts in federal health care funding could leave more people without access to routine exams, potentially leaving some with no option other than seeking care in emergency departments. While many nurses welcome the additional beds, the president of the Registered Nurses Professional Association said expanding capacity alone is not enough. “The county needs to step up and have more nurses so we will be able to accommodate the expansion,” association President Allan Kamara said. Regional Medical Center’s emergency department recently treated nearly 300 patients in a single day. Officials hope the expansion will help future patients receive treatment more quickly.

headlines.title: Benicia receives $40M from Valero refinery pollution penalties
headlines.description: A small East Bay community is receiving tens of millions of dollars after a local refinery polluted the air. The Bay Area Air District announced Thursday at a news conference at the Benicia Community Center that $30 million will go to the city, while the remaining $10 million will go to the local school district. The money comes from penalties paid by the Valero refinery after it settled claims that the facility exceeded emissions standards for more than 10 years. The refinery shut down in April. This marks the first time the Air District has reinvested fines directly into communities affected by pollution. NBC Bay Area’s Bob Redell has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: 49ers set to embark on NFL's longest road trip for season opener in Australia
headlines.description: The San Francisco 49ers got instructions for how to prepare for the longest road trip in NFL history as they get set to depart the Bay Area for Melbourne, Australia, late Wednesday night for the season opener against the Los Angeles Rams next week. They were given advice on how to eat and hydrate, what to do after arriving and the best options of when to sleep on the approximately 8,000-mile flight that will take about 16 hours and cross the international dateline that will make a Wednesday departure turn into a Friday arrival. Niners defensive lineman and avid world traveler Keion White has a simple approach. “I don’t know if you can OD on melatonin, but I’m going to try,” he said. “Take five melatonins, go to sleep on the plane. As soon as I wake up, I’m taking five more. Just keep rolling like that.” While some members of the 49ers organization, including coach Kyle Shanahan, have been lamenting the season-opening trip, White is embracing it after already playing games in Germany and London earlier in his career. He plans to watch TikTok before he arrives to get ideas of what to do and then get on public transportation and explore after team meetings on the first day to help make sure he stays up all day and gets onto a normal sleep schedule as quickly as possible. “I’m an experience guy,” he said. “If I’m up, walking around, just going to go do stuff, I’ll be up. Just go explore. We will have meetings and everything like that, but once I do that, I’m out exploring Melbourne and getting around town.” Both the 49ers and Rams studied the process intently in the offseason, even sending advance staffers to Australia to report back on how long it took to adjust to the time change. But they came up with far different answers leading up to the game on Sept. 11. The Niners will leave Wednesday night in California, arrive in Melbourne on Friday morning and then take time to adjust to the new time zone. They will hold a light practice on Saturday, take Sunday off and then have a normal stretch of three practices on Monday through Wednesday before playing the opener on Friday morning. They will leave right after the game and are expected to land back in the Bay Area on Friday afternoon. They then will be able to take the weekend off before preparing for the Week 2 game against Miami on Sept. 20. “It’s a big adjustment on the body,” Shanahan said. “So, the recommendation for everybody has been to tell us when to go, and it’s made a lot of sense. I know how our players feel also. I was a little bit on the fence. Science wasn’t and what I was reported on and our players weren’t at all. So that helped me get off the fence.” The Rams consulted with their own scientists and came up with the opposite approach. They will do most of their practice at home and aren’t expected to arrive in Australia until about 24 hours before the game, hoping the short stay leads to no jet lag. The better option might not be known until after the game. The approach by the Niners has made the past few days a whirlwind. The players got the weekend off after playing the final exhibition game on Thursday night in Las Vegas and resumed practice on Monday — the day after the roster was reduced to 53 players. The front office had to make those cuts, put together a practice squad and figure out which players would be healthy for Week 1 to make sure they had the correct roster in place before departing. “There’s a lot behind the scenes,” general manager John Lynch said. “Our logistics folks, our folks that work in the cafe, have just gone to tremendous lengths, our health and performance team, to make sure that we’re giving our players the best opportunity to feel right when they play down there in Australia. Everything from getting visas, which much more complicated than I ever knew, and they’ve been outstanding. … Hats off to those guys for pulling off a monumental task, and it’s not done yet.” Lynch said he had to make sure all the practice squad players he wanted to sign had passports with one needing his parents to send it overnight. It was an even bigger scramble for offensive lineman Jarrett Patterson, who was acquired in a trade from Houston on Sunday. “They were like, hey, do you have a passport? We’re leaving for Australia in three days,” he said. “I was like, ‘Whoa!’ It’s obviously a quick turnaround getting here a couple hours after I found out and now getting ready for Australia.” But in all, the players are welcoming the challenge and opportunity. Cornerback Deommodore Lenoir said he’d travel 30 hours if needed to play in an NFL game and rookie De’Zhaun Stribling has a must-see item on his to-do list before making his debut. “I kind of want to see a kangaroo, just because,” he said. “To see how big they are.” ___ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

headlines.title: Nvidia to spend $13 billion on Hugging Face, which will remain an open source platform
headlines.description: Chipmaker Nvidia is buying artificial intelligence software platform Hugging Face for $13 billion. It’s the latest deal by the company, whose processors are integral to the AI boom, and highlights Nvidia’s push to champion increasingly popular open-source AI models. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang wrote in a blog post Thursday that more than 18 million developers, researchers and creators use Hugging Face to share more than 3 million models, 500,000 data sets and 1 million applications. More than 200,000 companies also that use the platform, he said. In July, Hugging Face’s data processing systems were hacked, and ChatGPT maker OpenAI acknowledged that its artificial intelligence system was to blame, sending shock waves through the security community amid heightened concerns about the capabilities of powerful AI models. Just over a week later, Anthropic said its artificial intelligence models hacked into three other organizations during testing. That was followed closely by an announcement from Meta, which said its AI model accessed the internet on its own and hacked another company. The wave of AI intrusions occurred just a month after President Donald Trump signed an executive order creating a framework for the federal government to vet the national security risks of the most advanced AI systems for up to a month before their public release. On Thursday, however, Nvidia’s Huang said that Hugging face will remain an open platform. He signaled that Nvidia is betting that more businesses will turn to open-source AI, which lets them download and customize their own AI models, rather than pay for proprietary AI services from companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic. Open models let startups, businesses, universities and public institutions build on advanced capabilities without training every model from scratch,” Huang wrote in a blog post. “They enable organizations to match the right model to the right job. Hugging Face will still support multicloud and multi-accelerator development and deployment. Nvidia has released more than 500 models and more than 250 open data sets on Hugging Face. “Nvidia’s investment in Hugging Face is a strong strategic hedge against the different ways AI could evolve,” Bret Greenstein, chief AI officer at global business and technology consulting firm West Monroe, said in an emailed statement. “With much of Nvidia’s valuation tied to the adoption and expansion of AI over the next decade, the company has a clear interest in supporting the entire ecosystem’s success.” Nvidia’s high-end chips have emerged as the leading building blocks for AI, and are highly sought after. The Santa Clara, California-based company reported quarterly profits of $59.69 billion late last month. While AI has powered stock market gains and U.S. economic growth in recent years, there’s been growing skepticism about whether AI will justify the trillions of dollars being spent to develop the technology. The AI industry is also faces increasing pushback amid objections to the expansion of data centers and fears that the rapid speed of AI adoption could lead to widespread job losses worldwide. The $12.93 billion deal includes $1 billion for a retention plan for Hugging Face employees, Huang told CNBC. Nvidia’s shares rose nearly 2% in morning trading. Hugging Face is not publicly traded. ___ AP Business Writer Kelvin Chan contributed to this report.

headlines.title: Monterey County DA's Office clarifies details of infant death investigation
headlines.description: On Wednesday, the Monterey County District Attorney’s Office released a statement clarifying some details of the investigation into the dead infant found on the side of the road in August. On Monday, the Monterey County Sheriff’s Office said one of the suspects involved in the case was the infant’s 14-year-old mother; on Wednesday, however, the DA’s Office said it has “not received a filing request for criminal charges” against the minor. The DA’s Office explained that law enforcement obtained a Ramey warrant, which is issued by a judge based upon finding of probable cause. It added that, ultimately, the DA’s Office is responsible for determining whether charges will be filed. The DA’s Office said it , “recognizes the 14-year-old is a victim of her father’s abuse.” For that reason, if the teen is found, the DA’s Office said it’s District Attorney victim advocates and partner agencies will be ready to assist her, connect her with resources and ensure she receives the help she needs. “Whether she is currently able to seek assistance or not, we want her to know that help is available and that our office and our community partners are prepared to support her when she is able to access those services,” the DA’s Office wrote. On Aug. 1, at around 8:30 a.m., a newborn girl was found on the side of the road in the 100 block of Struve Road, authorities said. The sheriff’s office said the newborn was declared dead at the scene, and a postmortem forensic exam allegedly found that she had signs of traumatic injury. The DA’s Office said criminal charges were filed against the teen’s biological father, Sergio Galvez Perez, on suspicion of sexually assaulting the 14-year-old. Additionally, authorities said they are reviewing potential charges involving the teen’s mother, but noted these potential charges are unrelated to the death of the infant and unrelated to the sexual assault allegedly committed by Perez.
